recABS9cTyYGHFXEG.Body: The Sonic Slider is the flagship tool behind Biofield Tuning itself, a weighted tuning fork hand-tuned to 93.96 Hz, the twelfth harmonic of the Schumann Resonance, Earth's own natural electromagnetic pulse. Its extended handle lets you glide it smoothly across the face, neck, and body, and practitioners and users regularly report support for relaxation, circulation, and nervous system regulation. When Melissa joined Kyle Denton and me on InnerVerse, we explored the premise that spirit precedes form, and homeopathy demonstrates that principle as plainly as anything I know. RMDY makes quality remedies and first aid kits accessible, prepared with real care for who makes the medicine and how.

fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "Making Art for Yourself Every Day", "body": "Johnny Larson said he spent the lockdown year drawing daily on an iPad his friends talked him into buying. He explained that he once changed his style to sell art, felt like a hack when sales stopped, and then decided to make art for himself and trust that buyers would follow. Chance argued that attention poured into a creation amplified a person's spiritual currency, and he praised Johnny's steady flow. Johnny said he refused to explain what his drawings meant, preferring that viewers find their own meaning, and he described a Patreon and a Locals page built to keep his work off the big platforms."}, {"title": "Debugging the System and Political Theater", "body": "Chance relayed a metaphor from a video he had watched, in which corporations pay hackers to break their own systems, and he suggested that the world's distortion might be a hired team finding the bugs in life. Johnny called the idea interesting. He said he stayed optimistic because even untrained observers sensed that something was wrong, and he argued that people excused corruption whenever their own team held power. Chance likened the two sides to Coke and Pepsi, then pointed to a Telegram group that shares printable sticker designs as one way to answer propaganda."}, {"title": "Games, Comics and Where Attention Goes", "body": "Johnny said he worried about kids absorbed in long online games without real interaction, though he admitted he still loved playing. Chance argued that modern games imitated the way a person pours spiritual attention into a creation. Johnny also said Thanos was a rip off by the creators' own account and that he preferred Darkseid, whom he described as obsessed with the anti-life equation. Chance relayed Slick Dissident's mapping of twenty-two Marvel films onto the major arcana of the tarot, and argued that such mapping worked as a kind of spellcraft that mirrored nature's patterns."}, {"title": "Chance on Sound Healing and Biofield Tuning", "body": "Chance said he first heard Eileen Day McKusick on podcasts and felt a strong signal in early 2020 to pursue tuning forks. He described his earlier life as a rave wizard, waving selenite crystals to help festival-goers having a hard time. He argued that the biofield was a roughly six foot bubble space whose regions tended to carry similar meanings from person to person, and that the chart worked as a language even if it were purely conceptual. He said he asked his own higher self and other layers for help before sessions, and that the magic was electricity, not him."}, {"title": "Research Habits and Bearing Fruit", "body": "Chance played a clip from Weaving Spiders Welcome 46 in which a panelist compared early research to an infotainment buffet, then to cooking at home and grafting a first branch onto an apple tree. Chance said he had mostly absorbed information for years and only brought original research to his channels after working through a cyberpunk tarot with Lindsay. Johnny called himself an artist of all trades and said he took in information best by doodling while listening. Chance added that artists could reach the subconscious directly, sharing a feeling of awareness without listing every reference."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: Keeping on track with art, and forcing the flow state with maniacal dedication to doin' the thang, with the one and only Yeti Slang, Johnny Larson.
